core_concept: Externally subsidized breeding islands: penguins acquire trophic resources in the marine environment but reproduction is constrained by discrete terrestrial or sea-ice breeding substrates, allowing regional marine forcing to be separated from local breeding-patch filtering.

paper1_v1.title: Regional decline, local concentration: within-island reorganization of Adelie penguin breeding groups

paper2.working_title: Breeding-island architecture filters penguin population fate across Antarctica
paper2.status: Gate 0 passed for Pygoscelis trend lane; atlas design next
paper2.secondary_extension: 50-60 S sub-Antarctic islands only after an explicit data-coverage gate
paper2.geographic_scope: Antarctic-wide study domain with geographically uneven long-term monitoring
paper2.primary_modeling_strategy: species-specific Pygoscelis models first; cross-species synthesis second; pooled hierarchical model secondary and region-adjusted

paper2_question: When marine trophic resources lie outside the breeding patch, which properties of the breeding substrate determine whether regional environmental change is realized locally as persistence, decline, extinction, colonization or replacement?

paper2_hypotheses.H1_regional_forcing_local_fate: Population trajectories share regional components, but site fate retains predictable variation associated with breeding-site properties.
paper2_hypotheses.H2_habitat_option: After regional forcing is accounted for, the amount and heterogeneity of usable ice-free breeding habitat increase persistence by providing alternative breeding options during environmental deterioration.
paper2_hypotheses.H3_island_architecture: For terrestrial breeders, area alone is less informative than the geometry, relief, ice-free habitat amount, ecosystem heterogeneity and isolation of the breeding site.
paper2_hypotheses.H4_breeding_substrate_interaction: Effects of terrestrial island architecture are strongest for terrestrial-breeding Pygoscelis species and weak or absent for emperor penguins breeding on sea ice, providing a substrate-based negative-control comparison.
paper2_hypotheses.H5_palmer_generalization: The Palmer Paper 1 pattern of internal breeding-structure reorganization predicts that declining terrestrial colonies should show stronger local concentration or site loss where breeding-habitat options are fewer.

secondary_species_gate.status: insufficient for the primary south-of-60 trend lane
secondary_species_gate.rule: reserve for a separately contracted sub-Antarctic extension

new_user_constructed_dataset.name: Antarctic Penguin Breeding-Island Atlas
new_user_constructed_dataset.principle: MAPPPD/APBP supplies breeding-site anchors and demographic observations; island/breeding-site traits are newly derived in mina from independent spatial layers.
candidate_traits: distance to continental land or nearest large landmass

design_order: Gate 0 complete: inventory APBP/MAPPPD temporal and species coverage without fitting ecological models
freeze site-type rules and spatial trait extraction for the Pygoscelis atlas
build the Antarctic Penguin Breeding-Island Atlas outcome-blind
freeze demographic response eligibility, observation-method handling and trend/end-state definitions
only then join demographic outcomes and fit macroecological models
anti_p_hacking_rules: no selecting island traits because they correlate with observed population trends
no changing minimum time-series length after outcome effects are inspected
no redefining island versus continental sites using outcome information
no treating APBP site points as literal island polygons without spatial intersection
no claiming a tectonic Antarctic Plate boundary is equivalent to the biological study domain

substrate_contrast_extension.status: not viable in the same APBP nest-count trend lane
substrate_contrast_extension.evidence: 1 candidate trend-eligible site-species unit in the pinned MAPPPD inventory
substrate_contrast_extension.next_rule: open only with a separate frozen emperor demographic source or a different predeclared response such as occupancy/colony persistence

gate0_result.decision: proceed to outcome-blind breeding-island atlas construction

gate0_geography.design_consequence: species and region are partially confounded, especially for chinstrap and gentoo; do not make an unqualified pooled species x island-trait model the primary test
